patients.summary: Administrative assistant who joined in 2019 with hypothyroidism, asthma and quiet uveitis; over seven years outside specialists add a prolactinoma, seronegative RA, carpal tunnel, a right vestibular schwannoma, pemphigus vulgaris, RA-ILD and steroid-induced glaucoma.

documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller Judith Rosenblum, DOB 1/31/1976. Wants to move her primary care to us; her current office is losing her doctor to retirement this summer. Has thyroid and asthma meds she'll bring. Insurance PPO, card on file request sent. Booked new pt physical 6/11 at 9:00. Asked her to sign the records release so we can pull her old chart.

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
43 y/o woman establishing care. Transferring from a nearby internal medicine office; records release signed today.

PMH
- Hypothyroidism, on levothyroxine for >10 yrs. Dose 125 mcg for the last several years per her. Takes it with coffee some mornings, we talked about spacing it.
- Asthma for many years. On fluticasone-salmeterol 250/50 one inhalation BID and albuterol as needed, uses rescue maybe twice a month. Night symptoms rare. No ED visits or hospital stays for asthma in years. Needs a steroid burst once in a while.
- Chronic anterior uveitis, both eyes. Sees an outside ophthalmologist about yearly. Has needed steroid drops for flares in the past, nothing in over a year; eyes quiet now.

PSH: T&A at 12. Wisdom teeth out at 22.
Meds: as above.
Allergies: penicillin, sulfa antibiotics. Doesn't remember what happened with either, told as a child/young adult.
FH: mother with autoimmune thyroid disease. Father T2DM. Sister has lupus. Maternal aunt with RA.
SH: administrative assistant. Married. Smoked about half a pack a day for ~20 years, quit 2016 (~10 pack-years). Wine a glass or two a week. No drugs.
OB/GYN: never pregnant. Periods regular. Last Pap 2016 normal with negative HPV per her; mammogram last year normal.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: well appearing, BMI ~25.6. HEENT: conjunctivae white, PERRL, TMs clear, oropharynx clear. Neck: thyroid not enlarged, no nodules. Lungs clear, no wheeze, good air movement. Heart regular, no murmur. Abd soft, nontender. Ext no edema. Skin warm. Joints without swelling.

A/P
1. Hypothyroidism: continue levothyroxine 125 mcg; TSH today.
2. Moderate persistent asthma, well controlled on current regimen. Continue. Refills as needed.
3. Chronic anterior uveitis, quiescent; continue outside ophthalmology.
4. Health maintenance: CBC, CMP, lipids. One-time HCV and HIV screening, she agrees. Mammogram ordered. Pap due 2021. Colonoscopy at 45. Tdap 2014 per her, will confirm in old records. Flu shot in the fall.
5. Former smoker, 10 pk-yr, below the threshold for lung screening.
RTC 1 year for physical, sooner for asthma or thyroid.

documents.title: Your recent lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Judith, all of your labs from Tuesday look good: thyroid level is right where it should be on the 125, blood counts and kidney/liver tests are normal, cholesterol is fine, and the hepatitis C and HIV screens are negative. No changes. Nice to meet you.

documents.title: Office Visit - Asthma
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: About a week of wheezing and a tight chest, worse at night and climbing the stairs at work. Using albuterol 3-4 times a day the last few days, which helps for a couple of hours. No fever. Not coughing anything up. Taking her fluticasone-salmeterol twice daily, she says she hasn't missed doses. Has needed a few days of prednisone for similar spells before, last one maybe 2 years ago.
O: Comfortable, speaking full sentences. Vitals as recorded, sat normal on RA. Scattered expiratory wheeze both sides, moving air well. No accessory muscle use. Heart RRR.
A: Moderate persistent asthma with flare.
P: Prednisone 40 mg daily x 5 days, no taper. Continue controller BID, albuterol q4h prn. Reviewed when to go to the ED (rescue lasting <2h, can't talk in sentences, lips blue). Portal update in a week, sooner if not improving.

documents.title: Breathing update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Finished the prednisone Saturday. Way better, back to using the rescue inhaler maybe once a day and not at all yesterday. Slept through the night. Thank you!

documents.title: RE: Breathing update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great to hear. Keep the twice-daily inhaler going even when you feel well. Let me know if it flares again.

Eyes: saw ophthalmology in the winter, no uveitis activity.

Exam: Pleasant, NAD. Thyroid normal size. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Breasts without masses, no axillary nodes. Abdomen soft. Skin unremarkable. No joint swelling.

Plan:
- TSH, CBC, BMP today.
- Mammogram ordered.
- Pap due next year.
- Flu shot when it arrives in the fall.
- Discussed colonoscopy at 45 next year.
Return 1 yr.

Outside gastroenterology endoscopy center. Procedure date 8/10/2021.
Indication: first screening colonoscopy, age 45, no family history of colon cancer.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
First visit in over a year (missed June physical).

S: Exhausted for months, up ~6 kg since last summer without eating differently, always cold at work when others aren't. Since about April her hands go numb and tingle, mostly thumb, index and middle fingers both sides, wakes her at night and she shakes them out. Admits she's been skipping her levothyroxine most days for roughly a year, "fell off the routine" when she went back to the office. Asthma fine. No vision change, no headaches.

O: Weight 74 kg (68 in 2019). BP normal. Skin dry on the forearms and shins. Thyroid not palpable. Lungs clear.

A/P:
1. Hypothyroidism, likely undertreated from missed doses. She would like to see an endocrinologist this time; her mother's thyroid was managed by one and she wants help setting up the routine and checking whether the dose is right. Referral placed; she has an appt 10/25 and they will draw labs there. Restart levothyroxine 125 daily now, every morning.
2. Bilateral hand paresthesias, nocturnal. Will see how this does once thyroid is treated; endocrine will look too.
3. Flu shot today.
4. Reschedule physical in the spring; Pap at that visit.

documents.title: Endocrinology Consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology clinic. Date of service 10/25/2021.
Re: Judith Rosenblum, 45 F. Thank you for this referral.

She describes about half a year of numb, tingling fingers on both hands (thumb through middle finger) that is worse overnight and wakes her, along with tiredness, weight gain and feeling cold. Long history of hypothyroidism on levothyroxine 125 mcg, but by her own account she has taken it only sporadically over the past year.

Other history: asthma on ICS/LABA, chronic anterior uveitis (ophthalmology). Former smoker. Allergies: penicillin, sulfa drugs.
Family: mother with Hashimoto disease.

Exam: skin dry and coarse. Delayed relaxation phase of the ankle and biceps reflexes. Tinel's sign at both wrists produces finger tingling; Phalen's maneuver brings on her symptoms.

Labs today: TSH 12 mIU/L (ref 0.4-4.0). Free T4 0.5 ng/dL (ref 0.9-1.7).

Impression: overt hypothyroidism due to missed doses rather than an inadequate dose. The hand findings point to median nerve irritation at the wrist, which often improves as the thyroid is corrected; worth re-examining once she is euthyroid.

Plan: levothyroxine 125 mcg every morning, consistently. We set up a weekly pillbox and phone alarm. TSH in 6-8 weeks; she can draw at your lab. I will see her again in about six months.

documents.title: Pharmacy Immunization Notice
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Retail pharmacy notification: COVID-19 Pfizer booster given 11/13/2021. Entered in immunizations.

documents.title: Thyroid
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just wanted you to know I've been taking the thyroid pill every single day since the endocrinologist visit. Pillbox is working. Less tired already. They want a blood test in January, can I do it at your lab?

documents.title: RE: Thyroid
documents.author: RN
documents.body: That's great news. Yes, we have the endocrinologist's order on file. Walk in any weekday morning after the first week of January.

documents.title: TSH Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: TSH back in range after consistent dosing. Copy faxed to endocrinology. Portal note to pt: keep doing exactly what you're doing.

conditions.label: Prolactinoma
conditions.note: 1.7 cm sellar mass on MRI, per endocrinology

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet (0.5 mg) by mouth twice a week

documents.title: Pituitary tumor
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi. I wanted to let you know before the letter gets to you. I told the endocrinologist on Monday about my headaches and that my period stopped last fall and there's been milky stuff from both breasts. They did a blood test and an MRI the same week, it's a pituitary tumor that makes prolactin. They said it's not cancer and a pill usually shrinks it. I started cabergoline, one pill twice a week. Honestly kind of freaked out. Is there anything I should do from your end?

documents.title: RE: Pituitary tumor
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me, and I'm sorry this was a scary week. A prolactin-secreting pituitary tumor is one of the most treatable tumors there is, and cabergoline is the standard first treatment; most people do very well on it. Endocrinology will lead this. Take it with food at night if it makes you queasy. I've added it to your med list. Let's talk more at your physical in July, and call sooner if the headaches get worse or your vision changes.

documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology clinic, follow-up visit 5/9/2022 (letter delayed).

Judith returns about seven months after her first visit, now taking levothyroxine reliably. New since then: roughly six months of headaches that are getting worse, milky discharge from both nipples, and no menses for more than eight months. She has never been pregnant. She does not notice vision problems but says small print has become harder to read.

Exam: confrontation fields show a bitemporal deficit.

Results: prolactin 210 ng/mL. TSH and free T4 normal on the current dose. Pituitary MRI: a 1.7 cm mass in the sella that reaches and presses on the optic chiasm.

Assessment: prolactin-secreting pituitary macroadenoma with chiasmal contact; hypothyroidism now controlled.

Plan: cabergoline 0.5 mg twice weekly. Repeat prolactin in about 3 months and pituitary MRI after a year of treatment. Call for any sudden severe headache or worsening vision. Continue levothyroxine 125 mcg.

Allergies on file: penicillin, sulfa.

reports.text: Liquid-based cervical cytology, satisfactory for evaluation, transformation zone present. Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV not detected.
reports.conclusion: NILM; HPV negative. Co-test in 5 years.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
46F, annual.

Interval: endocrinology found a prolactinoma in May (1.7 cm, touching the chiasm), on cabergoline 0.5 twice weekly since. Headaches much less. Discharge slowing down. No period yet. Taking levothyroxine daily with the pillbox, energy better, weight down a little to 72. Asthma steady, one controller puff BID.

Exam: NAD. Thyroid normal. Lungs clear. Heart RRR. Breasts: no masses, no expressible discharge today. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions, Pap/HPV collected. Joints no swelling.

A/P
- Prolactinoma, improving symptomatically on cabergoline; endocrine following with prolactin and a repeat MRI.
- Hypothyroidism, controlled.
- Asthma, controlled.
- HM: Pap/HPV today. CBC, CMP, lipids. Mammogram ordered. Colonoscopy 2021 normal. Flu in fall. PHQ-9 3.
Back in a year, or sooner.

documents.title: Office Visit - Joint Pain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: hands and knees hurting.

HPI: Since around April her finger joints ache and are stiff on waking, it takes over an hour before she can type properly. Over the summer it spread to both wrists and now both knees. No rash, no fevers, no recent illness, no diarrhea, no urinary symptoms, no eye flare. Aunt on mother's side has RA, sister has lupus.

Exam: Swelling and tenderness over the MCPs and PIPs of both hands, symmetric. Wrists tender. Both knees warm with a small effusion, mild. No nodules. Skin clear, no psoriasis. Eyes white.

Assessment: symmetric inflammatory small-joint polyarthritis with knee involvement, 5 months.

Plan: ESR, CRP, RF, anti-CCP, ANA today with CBC and CMP. Referring to rheumatology.

documents.title: Your joint labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your inflammation markers are up (sed rate 50, CRP 25), which fits with what we saw in your joints. The rheumatoid factor, CCP antibody and ANA tests are negative; that doesn't rule out rheumatoid arthritis, since some people test negative. Blood counts and kidney/liver tests are normal. Rheumatology has your referral and these results.

documents.title: RE: Your joint labs
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks. They gave me Oct 25, earliest they had. Is it ok to wait?

documents.title: RE: Your joint labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, that's fine. Put yourself on their cancellation list.

documents.title: Rheumatology Consultation
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology practice. Visit 10/25/2022.

Ms. Rosenblum, 46, sent for joint pain. Six months of pain and morning stiffness lasting more than an hour, beginning in the fingers and moving to the wrists and then the knees. No recent infections, GI or GU symptoms. Background of hypothyroidism and a prolactinoma on cabergoline; asthma.

Exam: both hands with swollen, tender PIP and MCP joints; both knees with mild synovitis.

Labs (drawn by PCP 9/20): ESR 50 mm/hr, CRP 25 mg/L, RF negative, anti-CCP negative, ANA negative.

Impression: seronegative rheumatoid arthritis, active.

Plan:
- Methotrexate 20 mg orally once weekly, with folic acid 1 mg daily.
- No alcohol beyond an occasional glass; she drinks little.
- CBC with CMP every 4 weeks for 2 months, then every 3 months. Her PCP's lab is fine; please forward results.
- Inactivated vaccines encouraged, including pneumococcal.
- Return 3 months.
Allergies: PCN, sulfonamides.

documents.title: Nurse Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Labs for rheumatology (CBC, CMP, 2 wks into weekly methotrexate). Flu vaccine L deltoid, PCV20 R deltoid per PCP order since she's starting immunosuppression. No prior reactions. Pt says methotrexate day is Sunday, a little tired the next day but ok. Observed, no reaction.

documents.title: Orthopedics - Hand
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
Outside orthopedics and sports medicine group, hand clinic. DOS 4/26/2023.

47 y/o F with RA (rheumatology, on methotrexate) and earlier hand numbness evaluations. Three months of increasing finger stiffness, trouble with jars, steady dull ache at both wrists. Worst in the morning, makes dressing slow, loosens somewhat as the day goes on. Wedding ring is tighter. Occasional palm tingling.

Exam: swelling with tenderness at the 2nd and 3rd MCPs, both hands. Wrist flexion limited by pain. Tinel and Phalen maneuvers reproduce her paresthesias bilaterally.
Recent labs: normocytic anemia and an elevated CRP.

Impression: bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome in the setting of active RA synovitis.
Plan: prefabricated neutral wrist splints at night, both sides. MCP synovitis back to her rheumatologist. Return as needed.
Allergies: penicillin, sulfa.

documents.title: Good news from endo
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Endo appointment today. The MRI from last week shows the tumor is smaller and not touching the optic nerve anymore, and my prolactin is normal. Staying on the same cabergoline, see them in a year. Also the wrist splints at night are helping some.

documents.title: RE: Good news from endo
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's exactly what we hoped for. Glad the splints help. See you in July.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual visit.

Since last year: RA diagnosed in October (seronegative), on methotrexate 20 weekly and folic acid. Bilateral carpal tunnel per ortho in April, night splints help. Prolactinoma smaller on repeat MRI, prolactin normal per endo, same cabergoline. Thyroid fine. Asthma ok.

Feels her hands are the best they've been in a year; rheum says the flare settled.

Exam: BMI ~27. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Hands with minimal MCP puffiness, no synovitis of the knees today. Skin and mouth normal.

Plan:
- CBC/CMP for MTX, TSH, lipids today. April Hgb was 11.4, recheck.
- Shingrix #1 today given immunosuppression; #2 in 2 to 6 months.
- Mammogram ordered. Pap next due 2027.
- PHQ-2 1.
1 yr, or sooner.

events.reason: Right ear hearing loss and dizziness

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: For about 5 months she's had trouble hearing on the phone with her right ear, now switches to the left. Spells of the room spinning lasting minutes to an hour, a couple a month, no trigger she can find. Every so often the right side of her face feels numb. No ear pain or drainage. No new meds, nothing ototoxic.
O: Ear canals and TMs normal both sides. No nystagmus at rest. Face symmetric, strength normal.
A: Asymmetric right-sided hearing loss with episodic vertigo and right facial numbness.
P: ENT referral, they'll do audiometry. Return or ED for sudden worsening, weakness or severe headache. Shingrix #2 and flu shot today.

reports.text: Pure-tone audiometry with speech testing. Left ear: hearing within normal limits. Right ear: sensorineural hearing loss. Tympanograms type A both ears.

documents.title: Otolaryngology Consultation
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
Outside otolaryngology group. Seen 10/25/2023.

47-year-old woman (hypothyroidism, prolactinoma, rheumatoid arthritis, carpal tunnel syndrome) with six months of progressively worse hearing in the right ear and episodes of vertigo, plus intermittent numbness of the right face. No otalgia, otorrhea or ototoxic exposures.

Exam: Weber lateralizes to the left. Rinne positive (air better than bone) on both sides. Right corneal reflex and right facial sensation are decreased.
Audiometry: right sensorineural hearing loss.

Impression: asymmetric right SNHL with vertigo and trigeminal sensory signs; retrocochlear lesion must be excluded.
Plan: MRI brain with gadolinium, internal auditory canal protocol. Will call her with results.
Allergies: penicillin, sulfa drugs.

reports.study: MRI brain with and without contrast
reports.text: MRI brain without and with gadolinium, including thin-section imaging of the internal auditory canals. A 1.5 cm enhancing extra-axial mass sits at the right cerebellopontine angle and extends into the right internal auditory canal; no hydrocephalus. Left IAC normal. Small known pituitary adenoma within the sella, clear of the optic chiasm. Brain parenchyma otherwise normal; no acute infarct or hemorrhage.
reports.conclusion: Right cerebellopontine angle/internal auditory canal mass, 1.5 cm, consistent with vestibular schwannoma. Known small pituitary adenoma.

documents.title: Imaging Report Received
documents.author: MA
documents.body: MRI brain report from outside imaging center (ordered by ENT) received and routed to PCP.

documents.title: Ear MRI
documents.author: patient
documents.body: ENT called. They said it's an acoustic neuroma on the right, about 1.5 cm, benign. Their plan is to watch it and repeat the MRI in 6 months. I didn't really think of questions on the phone. Is watching it normal?

documents.title: RE: Ear MRI
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: I saw the report too. Yes, for a benign tumor of this size, watching it with repeat scans is a common and reasonable plan, because many of them grow very slowly or not at all. If it grows, there are good treatments. Write your questions down for the ENT follow-up, and let them or me know right away about sudden hearing loss, worse balance, facial weakness or bad headaches.

documents.author: RN
documents.body: CBC/CMP unremarkable. Copy to rheum.

documents.title: Office Visit - Mouth Sores
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Six weeks of sore mouth. Started as little blisters inside the cheeks that opened into raw patches and haven't healed; it hurts to eat anything crunchy or spicy, living on soup and yogurt. No skin blisters, no eye or genital sores. No fever. Methotrexate 20 weekly and folic acid daily, unchanged for over a year.
O: Several shallow erosions on both buccal mucosae, larger on the left, tender. Gums and tongue otherwise ok. No cervical nodes. Skin of face, trunk and arms clear.
A: Persistent painful oral erosions, not healing.
P: Urgent dermatology referral; office called and got her in on 4/23. Message to rheumatology. Soft bland diet, saltwater rinses. Call if blisters appear on the skin or she can't keep fluids down.

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (40 mg) by mouth every morning with food; taper as directed by dermatology

reports.text: Specimen: skin, trunk, punch biopsy, with separate specimen for direct immunofluorescence. Microscopic: intraepidermal blister with suprabasal cleavage and acantholytic keratinocytes; basal layer remains attached to the dermis. Direct immunofluorescence: intercellular IgG and C3 deposition throughout the epidermis.
reports.conclusion: Intraepidermal acantholytic blister with intercellular IgG and C3 on DIF, diagnostic of pemphigus vulgaris.

documents.title: Dermatology Consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Outside dermatology practice. Seen 4/23/2024, urgent referral.

48-year-old woman with RA, hypothyroidism and a pituitary adenoma. Two months of painful oral ulcers that began as small vesicles and enlarged into broad erosions, making eating difficult. In the past week, fragile blisters have appeared on her chest and back and break with minimal rubbing.

Exam: flaccid bullae on the trunk. Pressure at the edge of an intact bulla spreads it into neighboring normal-looking skin (positive Nikolsky). Crusted erosions on the buccal mucosa. No lymphadenopathy.

Labs: CBC, TSH and glucose normal. Desmoglein antibodies sent, pending.
Biopsy (see pathology): intraepidermal cleavage with acantholysis; DIF with intercellular IgG and C3.

Diagnosis: pemphigus vulgaris, mucocutaneous.

Plan: prednisone 40 mg daily, then a slow taper as lesions heal. TPMT activity drawn today; if normal, start azathioprine as a steroid-sparing agent and coordinate with rheumatology given methotrexate. Gentle skin care and bland mouth rinses. Follow-up in 2 weeks.
Allergies: penicillin, sulfa.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
48F, annual.

Big year: pemphigus vulgaris diagnosed in April (biopsy proven). Derm started prednisone 40 and then azathioprine 100 daily in May; she's now down to prednisone 10 mg daily per their taper. Mouth almost healed, skin clear except a few faded spots on the back. Still on methotrexate 20 weekly and folic acid for RA, joints quiet. Repeat ear MRI in May unchanged, ENT watching. Cabergoline and levothyroxine as before. Asthma controlled.

Weight up to 77 on the steroids, frustrated by it. Sleeping ok.

Exam: BP normal. Mild facial fullness. Oral mucosa with one small healing erosion, no new lesions. Skin of trunk with a few flat pink macules where blisters were, no bullae. Lungs clear. Heart RRR. Joints without synovitis.

Assessment/plan:
- Pemphigus vulgaris, improving on prednisone 10 and azathioprine; derm leads.
- Long-term glucocorticoid: start vitamin D3 1000 units daily, calcium from diet (she eats dairy daily), DXA baseline ordered. A1c today for steroid effect.
- RA on MTX, labs today with CBC/CMP. TSH.
- Prolactinoma stable. Acoustic neuroma under surveillance.
- HM: mammogram ordered. Flu and COVID in fall. Shingrix done. PCV20 done.
RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Office Visit - Dyspnea
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Since around the holidays she gets winded climbing the hill from the parking lot and on the stairs at home, slowly worse. Dry cough most days, nothing coming up. More tired than usual. No chest pain, no blood in sputum, no wheeze, albuterol doesn't change it. No fevers. Joints quiet; she hasn't missed methotrexate.
O: SpO2 93% on room air at rest. Afebrile. Fine crackles at both lung bases, no wheeze. Heart regular. No edema. No clubbing.
A: Progressive exertional dyspnea and dry cough with basilar crackles and lower saturation, in a patient with RA on methotrexate.
P: CXR tomorrow. Pulmonology referral, expedited. Return/ED for breathlessness at rest or chest pain.

reports.text: PA and lateral chest. Reticular opacities at both lung bases. Lung volumes preserved. No focal consolidation, effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size normal. Mediastinum unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Bibasilar reticular opacities. Recommend clinical correlation and further evaluation with CT as indicated.

documents.title: Pulmonology Consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary clinic. Visit date 4/21/2025.

Patient with rheumatoid arthritis, hypothyroidism and pemphigus vulgaris, referred for several months of gradually increasing breathlessness, dry cough and fatigue. She takes methotrexate faithfully and has had no recent joint flares. No chest pain, hemoptysis or wheezing.

Former smoker, 10 pack-years, quit 2016. Asthma on ICS/LABA. Allergies: penicillin, sulfa.

SpO2 93% on room air. Fine crackles at both bases.
Chest radiograph (3/25, reviewed): reticular opacities in the lower zones.
Pulmonary function testing today: restrictive physiology with a reduced diffusing capacity (DLCO).

Assessment: interstitial lung disease associated with rheumatoid arthritis.
Plan: high-resolution CT chest. Continue her current immunosuppressive regimen for now. Repeat PFTs with DLCO in 6 months. Return after the CT.

reports.text: High-resolution CT of the chest without contrast, inspiratory and expiratory prone and supine images. Subpleural reticulation at both lung bases. No honeycombing. No air trapping beyond normal. No nodules, consolidation or effusion. Normal heart size; no lymphadenopathy.
reports.conclusion: Basal subpleural reticulation without honeycombing, pattern consistent with nonspecific interstitial pneumonia.

documents.title: Ophthalmology Visit
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Outside ophthalmology practice. Date of visit 4/27/2026.

50-year-old woman with chronic anterior uveitis, on prednisolone acetate 1% drops for about six months since an autumn flare. Three months of slowly worsening side vision in both eyes. No pain, no redness.

Exam:
VA 20/25 OD, 20/25 OS.
No cataract. Anterior chambers quiet, no active uveitis.
IOP (applanation) 28 mmHg OD, 27 mmHg OS.
Dilated fundus exam: enlarged cup-to-disc ratio in both eyes.
Visual fields: peripheral field loss both eyes.

Assessment: open-angle glaucoma, steroid response, both eyes. Uveitis quiet.

Plan: start latanoprost 0.005% one drop both eyes at bedtime. Reduce prednisolone acetate to one drop both eyes once daily. IOP check in 6 weeks.
Allergies noted: penicillin, sulfonamides. Asthma noted.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up, first visit since the glaucoma diagnosis.

Eyes: ophthalmology in late April found pressures of 28/27 with cupping and field loss, called it steroid-response glaucoma. Started latanoprost at bedtime and cut the prednisolone drops to once daily. At the 6-week check in June the pressures were in the high teens per her, uveitis quiet. Vision about the same.
Asthma: one flare in January, prednisone 5 days, fine since.
ILD: stable per pulmonology, same exertional limit.
RA: MTX 20 weekly, folic acid, quiet.
Pemphigus: in remission on azathioprine 100.
Thyroid/pituitary: levothyroxine 125, cabergoline 0.5 twice weekly.
Med reconciliation done with her bottles: list updated.

Exam: Weight 73. BP normal. Conjunctivae white. Mouth and skin clear. Fine bibasilar crackles, no wheeze. Heart RRR. Joints quiet.

A/P
- Steroid-induced open-angle glaucoma: on latanoprost; per ophthalmology.
- Chronic anterior uveitis: prednisolone drops daily.
- RA-ILD, RA, pemphigus: continue current immunosuppression, specialists following.
- Hypothyroidism, prolactinoma, vestibular schwannoma surveillance, asthma: stable.
- CBC, CMP, TSH today.
Next visit end of September.
